# Traefik — custom-context-sse

App on /app context, proxy preserves the path, PUSH over Server-Sent Events with the client's Upgrade header stripped by a headers middleware.

Proxy URL on `http://localhost:9090`: `/app/`

## Configuration

See [docker-compose.yml](./docker-compose.yml) for service definitions.

Traefik dynamic config (`vaadin.yml`), mounted into
`/etc/traefik/dynamic`:

```yaml
# App on the /app context, proxy preserves the same path, PUSH over
# Server-Sent Events through a proxy that cannot upgrade a connection.
#
# The no-websocket middleware is what makes it "cannot": Traefik has no way to
# omit upgrade support, so the client's Upgrade and Connection headers are
# stripped before the request reaches the backend. Atmosphere then answers 501
# to a WebSocket transport, which is the point of the scenario.
http:
  routers:
    vaadin:
      # Two clauses, not a bare PathPrefix(`/app`). Traefik's PathPrefix is a
      # raw string prefix, so the bare form also matches /application. Every
      # context-prefix rule in this tree is written this way.
      rule: PathPrefix(`/app/`) || Path(`/app`)
      entryPoints:
        - web
      middlewares:
        - no-websocket
        - compress
      service: vaadin

  services:
    vaadin:
      loadBalancer:
        servers:
          - url: http://vaadin:8080

  middlewares:
    # Traefik upgrades on every route, so the only way to build a proxy that
    # cannot is to remove the client.s upgrade intent. An empty value deletes
    # the header rather than setting it empty.
    no-websocket:
      headers:
        customRequestHeaders:
          Upgrade: ""
          Connection: ""

    compress:
      compress:
        excludedContentTypes:
          - text/event-stream
          - text/plain
```

The entryPoints and the file provider come from the shared
[traefik.yml](../../traefik.yml), mounted read-only.
